bottom: Shapiro had raised about $55 million since the start of 2025 by the September 14, 2026 report, per [Spotlight PA](https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2026/10/josh-shapiro-stacy-garrity-pennsylvania-governor-debate-elections/), and his campaign says more than $60 million since he took office, per the [Inquirer](https://inquirer.com/politics/pennsylvania/josh-shapiro-campaign-fundraising-reelection-20260922.html). His Republican opponent Stacy Garrity had a bit over $5 million. Through early June 2026 he had more than 45,000 contributors, an average gift of $848, 82 donors at $100,000 or more, and 51 percent of his dollars from outside Pennsylvania, per [Public Source via the Capital-Star](https://penncapital-star.com/election-2026/heres-what-shapiros-huge-edge-over-garrity-in-national-campaign-contributions-looks-like/). The money is broad, so no single bloc dominates. Four interests combine large money with a live decision on his desk:

**Labor unions.** At least $1.6 million in named 2026 union checks from the Carpenters, IBEW Local 98, AFSCME and the teachers union. Live levers: transit money tied to his skill game tax, the FY 2027 to 2028 budget, and whether Pennsylvania opts in to the new federal tax credit scholarships.

**National Democratic and billionaire money.** The Democratic Governors Association at $1.25 million this summer, Michael Bloomberg at $2.5 million in 2025, Chris Larsen at $1 million in March 2026. The lever is political rather than regulatory: party building through $5.7 million he moved to the state party, and an open 2028 question he sidestepped at the October 7 debate.

**Gambling.** Casino parity on skill games is his stated position, a 52 percent tax worth almost $800 million in year one, per the [Inquirer](https://www.inquirer.com/politics/pennsylvania/pa-skill-games-lobbying-lawsuits-illegal-20260710.html). Fanatics owner Michael Rubin gave $78,200 in in-kind travel, and skill game operator PACs also gave in the summer period, amounts not stated.

Garrity had raised a bit over $5 million since the start of 2025 by the September 14 report, against about $55 million for Josh Shapiro, per [Spotlight PA](https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2026/10/josh-shapiro-stacy-garrity-pennsylvania-governor-debate-elections/). She entered the final stretch with about $1.4 million and had spent about $440,000 on advertising in the summer period, $204,000 of it on TV, per [Public Source](https://penncapital-star.com/election-2026/have-you-seen-a-garrity-ad-shapiro-leads-43-to-1-in-broadcast-digital-buys/). Her money is mostly in state and small. About 86 percent came from Pennsylvania and her average gift was $457. Three interests combine money with a live decision:

**The skill game industry.** She accepted a $33,500 flight from Pace-O-Matic founder Michael Pace. The company's PAC gave her $5,000. Her largest donor network, Bob Asher and his PA Future Fund at $345,000 in named 2026 gifts, runs through a man wire copy describes as a registered Pace-O-Matic lobbyist. Citizens Alliance, funded by Pace-O-Matic, pledged 750,000 doors for her. She backs the industry's flat $500 per machine fee.

**The Yass school choice network.** Commonwealth Leaders Fund and Commonwealth Children's Choice Fund gave her $720,000 across her treasurer races, about a fifth of that money, and Commonwealth Leaders Fund gave again in 2026. She would opt in to federal tax credit scholarships on day one.

**The Republican establishment.** Congressional committees, county parties, House GOP leader Jesse Topper and 2022 candidate Dave White form her second funding base, with a Mar-a-Lago fundraiser in spring 2026.

D.t: Josh Shapiro leads by 20.8 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 1,261,797 votes; a one point swing is about 30,288 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +14.6 and D +27.2. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +23.5. Your best recent poll is Bravo Group/PennLive at D +28.8; your worst is Z to A Research (D) at D +17.8. 8 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Philadelphia, a projected net 494,380 votes; Allegheny, a projected net 287,856 votes; Montgomery, a projected net 213,551 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Lancaster, D +5.0, 4.1% of the vote; York, R +3.4, 3.5% of the vote; Westmoreland, R +4.1, 3.0% of the vote; Berks, D +9.8, 2.9% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Josh Shapiro runs furthest behind in Franklin, Philadelphia, Lebanon. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 84% of voters, 55 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.21 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 72% of voters, 58 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.61 points; Voters without a degree, 60% of voters, 57 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Josh Shapiro: Immigration voters 30 to 67, Small counties 34 to 64, Midsize counties 48 to 49. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$19.8M cash against $1.3M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Registered Democrats cast 66% of the 890,346 ballots in Pennsylvania so far, against 25% for the other party. That is 2.2 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.7 points away from Josh Shapiro. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
